This is the runtime face of the `EXEC` vs `DYN` distinction the header made. And it names a choice this book has made quietly for two chapters: the CFI and canary demos all built with `-no-pie` "to keep printed addresses stable across runs" — non-PIE is exactly a binary whose base the kernel does not randomize.
RELRO: making the GOT read-only

The region PIE leaves writable is the GOT. In a PIE executable, calls to imported functions go through `.got.plt`, whose slots the loader writes — eagerly, or lazily on first call. A writable GOT is a standing target for the GOT-overwrite class of attack. RELRO (relocation read-only) is the linker/loader's answer: a `PT_GNU_RELRO` segment lists the ranges the loader flips to read-only after relocation is done. Read the two PIE builds the way `checksec` does — the RELRO segment, the section offsets, the dynamic flags:

$ llvm-readelf-23 -lW pie_pie | grep GNU_RELRO
  GNU_RELRO      0x0007c0 0x00000000000027c0 0x00000000000027c0 0x0001e8 0x000840 R   0x1
$ llvm-readelf-23 -SW pie_pie | grep -E '\.got|\.data'
  [20] .got              PROGBITS        0000000000002980 000980 000028 00  WA  0   0  8
  [22] .data             PROGBITS        00000000000039a8 0009a8 000014 00  WA  0   0  8
  [24] .got.plt          PROGBITS        00000000000039c0 0009c0 000028 00  WA  0   0  8
$ llvm-readelf-23 -lW pie_fullrelro | grep GNU_RELRO
  GNU_RELRO      0x0007c0 0x00000000000027c0 0x00000000000027c0 0x000220 0x000840 R   0x1
$ llvm-readelf-23 -SW pie_fullrelro | grep -E '\.got|\.data'
  [20] .got              PROGBITS        0000000000002990 000990 000028 00  WA  0   0  8
  [21] .got.plt          PROGBITS        00000000000029b8 0009b8 000028 00  WA  0   0  8
  [23] .data             PROGBITS        00000000000039e0 0009e0 000014 00  WA  0   0  8
$ llvm-readelf-23 -d pie_fullrelro | grep FLAGS
  0x000000000000001e (FLAGS)        BIND_NOW
  0x000000006ffffffb (FLAGS_1)      NOW PIE

In the default PIE build the RELRO segment covers `[0x27c0, 0x27c0 + 0x1e8)` = `[0x27c0, 0x29a8)`: `.init_array`, `.dynamic`, and `.got` — but not `.got.plt`, which sits at `0x39c0` next to `.data`, outside the segment. There is no `BIND_NOW`: the jump slots bind lazily on first call, and the table stays writable. That is the surface partial RELRO leaves open. Add `-Wl,-z,relro,-z,now` (full RELRO) and two things happen at once: the dynamic section gains `BIND_NOW`, so every jump slot is resolved at load time, and the linker physically moves `.got.plt` — from `0x39c0` to `0x29b8`, right after `.got`, inside the widened segment, whose end (`0x27c0 + 0x220 = 0x29e0`) is exactly `.got.plt`'s end. After the loader finishes, both GOT tables are read-only; a write to a jump slot faults.

items: IR: nothing. `-pie` and `-no-pie` produce byte-identical modules (at -O0 and -O2), and the flag warns as unused on the IR path. An IR pass can neither express nor detect the position model.
ELF: everything. `Type` (`EXEC` vs `DYN`), `(FLAGS_1) PIE`, and the relocation set (library-only vs library + `R_X86_64_RELATIVE` self-relocations) fully determine the load behavior.

Loader: the base. With ASLR on (`randomize_va_space = 2` here), the PIE base changes on every `exec`; the `-no-pie` base is the fixed file address. The in-image layout — offsets like `0x2288` — is invariant either way.

Linker: the RELRO boundary. Full RELRO (`-z now`) moves `.got.plt` inside the `PT_GNU_RELRO` segment and binds the jump slots eagerly, so both GOT tables are read-only after load; the default PIE build leaves `.got.plt` writable for lazy binding.

The compiler chooses the relocation model, the linker writes the `Type`, the `FLAGS_1` tag, and the RELRO segment, and the loader picks the base and binds the GOT, after every IR pass has run. The right tool for this hardening is a build flag, and the right verification is `readelf` plus a runtime address probe. The part's standard — judge the final artifact — lands here in its most literal form: the artifact is the executable, and the hardening lives in its header.

Checkpoint: (a) The -no-pie and -pie builds of the fixture have byte-identical IR. What records the position decision in the two executables instead — name the header field and the dynamic-section tag. (b) The PIE executable's relocations include a type the -no-pie executable lacks, used for the executable's own writable slots. Name the type, state the value the loader writes, and name the slots it fills in this fixture. (c) Full RELRO closes the one region the default PIE build leaves writable. Which section is it, what does the linker do to it in the full-RELRO build, and which dynamic-section flag comes with the change?

items: (a) The ELF header's `Type` field: `EXEC` (the fixed-address executable, mapped at its recorded file addresses) versus `DYN` (the position-independent object the loader maps like a shared library), plus the dynamic section's `(FLAGS_1) PIE` tag on the PIE executable. Nothing in the IR marks the decision — the two modules are byte-identical.

(b) `R_X86_64_RELATIVE`: the loader writes `load_base + offset` (the records read `*ABS*+0x16e0` and so on) into the executable's own writable slots — here the `.fini_array` entry at `0x27c0`, the `.init_array` entry at `0x27c8`, and a `.data` slot at `0x39b0`; the `.got` is not among them, its library slots still coming from the `GLOB_DAT` records both builds carry. The self-relocations exist only in the PIE executable, because its own base — and therefore its own addresses — is randomized at load time.

(c) `.got.plt`, the jump table lazy binding fills: in the default build it sits at `0x39c0` next to `.data`, outside the RELRO segment, so it stays writable. The full-RELRO linker moves it to `0x29b8`, inside the widened `PT_GNU_RELRO` segment (whose end is exactly `.got.plt`'s end), and the dynamic section gains `BIND_NOW`, so every jump slot is resolved eagerly at load. After load, the whole RELRO range — both GOT tables — is read-only, and a write to a jump slot faults.
